subject: Private VPC plane orchestration + annotated diagrams — review and evidence
messages:
From: Suren Patel <suren@clearsky.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC orchestration diagrams (first pass)

Hi Rachel / Irene,

Thanks again for the runthrough this morning. Per our call, attached are the annotated diagrams showing the suggested control-plane / data-plane separation for the Acme private deployment. Highlights:

- Control plane lives in a customer-managed VPC with a lightweight proxy in the edge cluster for cert propagation.
- Data plane inference nodes run in a separate subnet with dedicated egress NAT and an observability sidecar.
- KV cache keepalive and prefix cache are routed via the east-west overlay; we call out the BGP session for cross-site failover.

Please review the two attachments: annotated-diagrams_v1.pdf (visual callouts) and network-policy-matrix.xlsx (policy table). We tried to keep fallbacks minimal and documented the HA paths.

Ask: can you confirm whether Redwood requires an mTLS terminator in the customer control plane or if the edge proxy approach is sufficient for your compliance team? Also note we included a suggested DocuSign link for the site-specific SLA redlines (placeholder).

Thanks,
Suren
Solutions Architect, Clearsky

Attachments: annotated-diagrams_v1.pdf (pdf - 2.3MB), network-policy-matrix.xlsx (xlsx - 120KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Suren Patel <suren@clearsky.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC orchestration diagrams (first pass)

Suren — thanks for sending this over and for the clear diagrams. Quick notes after a skim:

1) Control plane termination: our compliance baseline expects key material to remain customer-owned. The edge proxy pattern is acceptable if the proxy never stores private keys and cert rotation is triggered from the customer KMS (we'll need evidence of the rotation workflow).

2) Observability sidecar: good, but add a note that telemetry egress must be routed through an observability-bastion (no direct public endpoints).

3) BGP session for failover: acceptable, but we need an ops-runbook snippet showing how to fail traffic to the secondary site and how the inference KV cache is cold-started safely.

Can Irene and I get a revised diagram with a callout for the KMS rotation path and a short ops snippet? Marissa — I'll loop you in for the SLA/contract impact if the customer requests the additional evidence.

If possible, Suren, send the ops-runbook snippet as a short text block in reply — we can drop that into the network-policy-matrix as a new tab.

Best,
Rachel
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Rachel + Suren. I reviewed the PDFs and added inline comments (see embedded callouts in annotated-diagrams_v1.pdf). High-level follow-up from my side:  

- KMS rotation: acceptable if customer provides a retained rotation log and automated rotation lambda that signals the edge proxy; we need a minimal acceptance test: rotate cert -> verify no token leakage across cache shards.
- mTLS terminator: Redwood does not require keys to leave the customer boundary. The proxy approach is fine provided we document the circuit:
  - Control-plane API endpoint -> edge proxy (TLS passthrough) -> ingress terminator in customer VPC with cert only seen by ingress.
- KV cache warmup: ops-runbook should call out a staggered warmup to avoid token storms; propose per-shard randomized backoff.

Suren, could you paste a 6–8 line ops-runbook snippet (psuedo-steps) into a reply and we will fold it into the policy matrix sheet. Marissa, if the customer asks for SLA exception language around rotation proof, I'll defer to legal but want to capture the ask now.

Cheers,
Irene
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Private VPC orchestration diagrams (first pass) — ops snippet and revised attachments

Forwarding updated assets and a short ops-runbook snippet as requested. I also looped in Acme Contracts for transparency on the SLA items.

Ops snippet (paste):
1) Pre-cutover: verify cert rotation endpoint responds and push test cert to edge proxy (validate SHA256).
2) Warmup phase: initiate KV shard warmups in waves of 10% nodes with randomized 0-30s jitter.
3) Failover: advertise BGP secondary route, wait for 30s stabilization, verify KV checksum parity.
4) Rollback: if checksum mismatch, drain new traffic and trigger cache-rebuild script per shard.
5) Evidence collection: upload rotation logs and cache checksum reports to the shared drive folder above.

Attachments: annotated-diagrams_v1-rev.pdf (pdf - 2.5MB), network-policy-matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx - 140KB)

Suren
